root_cause.statement: The ICE (tmem_copy handle live across scf.for boundary) is caused by the kernel's OWN TMEM lifecycle: the TMEM accumulator handle (tmem.retrieve_ptr + tcgen05.make_tmem_copy) is bound OUTSIDE the cutlass.range() loop and captured as an SSA value across the scf.for region boundary. The MLIR lowering fails to legalize the materialization from tmem_load atom to tiled_copy when that value crosses a scf.for/scf.yield boundary. This is NOT a DSL wall: the same pinned cutlass-dsl 4.5.2 wheel contains mamba2_ssd.py, which runs 4 tcgen05 MMAs per kernel including an inter-chunk recurrence via ONE alloc + static per-accumulator column offsets + ONE relinquish at the end of the entire kernel. Our bisect matrix never varied per-accumulator TMEM offsets — all bisect variants allocated a single 512-column block and used a single accumulated result, so the offset-partition approach was never tested.
root_cause.evidence_for_nvidia_precedent: nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.5.2 wheel ships mamba2_ssd.py with 4 tcgen05 MMAs per kernel using one alloc + static column offsets + one relinquish; this is the pattern to emulate
root_cause.fix_direction: loopfix idiom (re-derive TMEM handle INSIDE loop body) clears the ICE on the decoupled gemm repro (session-record); ultimate fix for run_k1_incB2 is one alloc + per-accumulator offset partition + one relinquish (matching mamba2_ssd.py)

next_probe.description: Box burst 1: (a) verify libcute_dsl_runtime.so md5 matches known-good 4.5.2 wheel (rules out silent .so mismatch, task #3259); (b) two-GEMM TMEM-offset probe: single alloc(512), two GEMMs using accumulator at column offsets 0 and 64 respectively, distinct mbarriers, one relinquish at kernel end; test in three sub-modes: independent (no data dependency between GEMMs), dependent (GEMM-2 reads GEMM-1 accumulator), looped (both inside cutlass.range(nt)). GO on any sub-mode = confirms the offset-partition route is viable for run_k1_incB2.
